Read units measure how much data a query reads (scans), in units of 4 KB. For example, if you have a table with 5000 rows, with each row ~200 bytes, and run a SELECT * FROM table, your query would scan (5000 rows * 0.2KB / 4KB read unit) 1000 KB in total, or 250 read units.

Write units measure how much data was written to a D1 database, in 1KB units. An INSERT of a single row of 1900 bytes — a userID, name, email address and comments field, for example — would count as two (2) write units (2KB).
Both read and write units are rounded up to the nearest whole unit. A query that reads 1,000 rows of approximately 90 bytes ( 1000*.009 / 4), would consume 23 read units.
